rule: GOAL: Fill four slots to match the color order shown in the top row. CONTROLS: Click a palette color to select it, then click a slot to place it. RULE: Slots must match the top row sequence exactly, from left to right. TRAP: Assuming the palette order matches the target order; it does not.

GOAL: Drop the magenta block into a yellow cup. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blue paddle horizontally; Space releases the block. RULE: The paddle catches the block only when positioned directly underneath it. TRAP: Believing the block falls straight down regardless of paddle position wasted time on missed catches.

GOAL: Navigate the player through the wall gap to touch all blue squares. CONTROLS: Click anywhere to move the player directly toward that spot. RULE: Movement is strictly horizontal and vertical, never diagonal. TRAP: Assuming clicks move the player diagonally wastes turns; plan straight lines to the gap first.

GOAL: Reach the far corner by sliding across the ice. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push you in that direction until you hit a wall. RULE: You cannot stop mid-slide; you only halt when blocked by an obstacle. TRAP: Thinking one press equals one tile step; you often fly past your target and must bank off walls to correct your path.

GOAL: Guide the token to the ball without exceeding the action limit. CONTROLS: Click a grid cell to move the token toward that point. RULE: Each click moves the token six cells and consumes bar energy. TRAP: Assuming dots are obstacles; they are just the trail left behind.

GOAL: Make the top and bottom switch rows match the yellow plug's prong pattern. CONTROLS: Click switches to toggle their horizontal or vertical dash states between visible and hidden. RULE: The level completes only when the switch configuration visually aligns with the plug's orientation. TRAP: Trying to make all switches identical or "all on" wastes time; only the specific prong-matching pattern counts.

GOAL: Rotate each column's pattern to match a target sequence before the timer expires. CONTROLS: Left/Right arrows move the cursor; Up/Down arrows rotate the current column's pattern. RULE: Patterns cycle in a fixed seven-step order, so choose the shorter rotation direction for each column. TRAP: Assuming all columns share the same rotation cycle wastes time; check each column's specific sequence length.

GOAL: Place the correct colors into the split red and green boxes to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Click a slot to select its piece, then click another to swap them. Press Space to test the solution. RULE: The green box inserts itself into the red sequence at the pipe's location, shifting the remaining red slots to the end. TRAP: Assuming the boxes fill independently or left-to-right ignores the pipe's interrupting role in the color order.

GOAL: Fill the bottom bar by placing three distinct blocks into their designated slots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; Space absorbs or deposits a block. RULE: Blocks are carried above the head and deposited exactly where the player stands. TRAP: Assuming blocks can be placed anywhere; they must align perfectly with the empty slots.

GOAL: Align your character with the wall gap to pass through. CONTROLS: Left and right moves shift your position; clicking blue tiles rotates or opens wall sections. RULE: You win when your character overlaps the gap in the outer boundary. TRAP: Thinking you must be perfectly centered; being slightly off-center still works if you touch the opening.

GOAL: Match the target pattern in every yellow slot by cycling through available glyphs. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the cursor between slots; the up arrow cycles the current slot's glyph. RULE: Only the slot under the cursor changes when you cycle; moving the cursor does not alter any glyph. TRAP: Assuming your screen data updates automatically after each move can cause you to misread the board; always verify the current state before acting.

GOAL: Fill three boxes in a specific sequence to match the target row. CONTROLS: Click a color in the bottom palette, then click a slot in a box. Press space to submit. RULE: Read the target left-to-right; slots fill in that order across all boxes, not by box group. TRAP: Thinking you must fill each box completely before moving to the next.

GOAL: Reach the exit tile safely. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one step. RULE: The guard moves only after you move each turn. TRAP: Believing the guard moves first leads to instant death when you step into its charging range.

GOAL: Fill all red and green slots to match the target sequence exactly. CONTROLS: Click a palette piece to select it, then click a board slot to place it; press space to submit. RULE: The outlined pipe piece splits the sequence, forcing the pre-filled green item to land at its specific target position. TRAP: Assuming the pipe is just decoration; it actually acts as a divider that shifts all subsequent items to new slots.

GOAL: Merge two pieces into a Y-shape, then move the result into the target zone. CONTROLS: Click empty cells to pull the nearest piece within range; click the target zone to deliver. RULE: A click pulls every piece within six squares, merging them if multiple are close enough. TRAP: Thinking you must merge at the target; you can merge anywhere, then move the combined piece once.

GOAL: Place pieces to create a continuous target sequence from the palette. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, then click board slots to place; press Space to verify. RULE: Pipes connect adjacent red slots, merging them so the blue box must match the resulting combined sequence. TRAP: Assuming pipes are optional or decorative; they are essential connectors that define the required pattern.

GOAL: Turn four edge tiles green to complete a diamond while the cap sits at the far right. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cap; clicks toggle tile colors. RULE: Clicks only work when the cap aligns with the target tile’s column. TRAP: Assuming any tile can be clicked regardless of cap position wastes actions on no-ops.

GOAL: Reach the exit after clearing the deadly hazard. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one tile at a time. RULE: Stepping directly onto the hazard destroys it instantly, removing the threat. TRAP: Avoiding the hazard wastes time; you must walk into it to neutralize it.

GOAL: Assign each colored pipe to its matching container to build a complete, ordered sequence of three. CONTROLS: Drag palette pipes to empty slots, then press space to verify the final arrangement. RULE: The fixed first pipe in each container reveals the required color order for that group. TRAP: Assuming you can mix pipe types within a container; each group must contain only its own color.

GOAL: Translate the yellow code "AJKJFLCC" into the corresponding blue glyph sequence using the provided symbol table. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to cycle the shape displayed in each blue slot until it matches the required glyph. RULE: Each blue slot must independently display the exact glyph assigned to its corresponding letter in the yellow code. TRAP: Assuming the blue glyphs change automatically or that you must press a button to submit the translation; you must manually set each slot.

ESTABLISHED: The wire is a rigid horizontal piston attached to the base’s center, moving vertically along a fixed rail. FAILED: Releasing blocks at the leftmost slot or base-aligned rows did not clear the level or trigger completion. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching blocks in order, holding them simultaneously, or delivering them to the left edge. CONTROLS: Vertical movement raises or lowers the base; the piston extends horizontally to push or collect blocks.

GOAL: Arrange nested boxes and pipes so the final symbol lands on the locked slot. CONTROLS: Drag symbols and pipes into empty slots, then press space to test the sequence. RULE: Pipes redirect the reading order to their target box before continuing with the current box's remaining slots. TRAP: Assuming pipes must stay in the starting box; placing them in other boxes changes the reading order to fit the target.

GOAL: Merge two nearby tokens, then deliver the merged and remaining tokens to their matching side blobs. CONTROLS: Clicking within a token’s range moves it toward the click; clicking between two close tokens merges them into a larger token. RULE: Merge first to create a larger token with a longer movement range, reducing total clicks needed for delivery. TRAP: Assuming you must deliver tokens individually before merging; delaying the merge wastes clicks on short-range movements.

GOAL: Extend two pistons to touch a central red target. CONTROLS: Click box sides to extend or retract each piston. RULE: Pistons move in fixed three-pixel steps toward the target. TRAP: Assuming exact pixel alignment is needed; stopping adjacent to the target counts as contact.

GOAL: Transform the bottom blue row into yellow. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the row left or right. RULE: Each blue shape matches a source in the Pink-to-Yellow examples, so map it directly to its paired yellow shape. TRAP: Assuming you needed to chain transformations through the Pink-to-Yellow and Source-to-Pink dictionaries separately, rather than recognizing the blue row already contained the correct source shapes for the direct lookup.

GOAL: Align the yellow cross and the blue cross with their respective target squares. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active cross three spaces per press. Spacebar switches focus between the yellow and blue crosses. RULE: The cross is a plus-shape; its center and arms must all cover the target box to lock it. TRAP: Assuming the center alone matters. You must position the cross so its entire vertical and horizontal arms overlap the target, not just the middle.

GOAL: Aligning all colored shapes into their target positions. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches to the next color. RULE: Diagonal lines are not connected, making each pixel a separate piece. TRAP: Believing diagonal pixels form a solid block, leading to wasted moves trying to move them as one unit.

GOAL: Place the largest purple square into the empty ring. CONTROLS: Click any piece to slide it along the trail toward the ring. RULE: Pieces shift sequentially; clicking a lower piece pushes the upper pieces forward. TRAP: Believing clicks swap adjacent pieces directly; they actually push the entire line down.

GOAL: Rotate the tile ring to place the target color on the marked corner. CONTROLS: Click left or right arrows to shift the ring clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Each click moves every tile one step along the loop. TRAP: Believing tiles move individually wastes time; the entire ring rotates as one unit.

GOAL: Reduce the board to a single remaining peg. CONTROLS: Click a peg to see valid moves, then click the destination to jump. RULE: A jump must land on an empty spot two spaces away, removing the jumped peg. TRAP: Assuming any adjacent peg can be jumped; you strictly need an empty space immediately beyond it.

GOAL: Guide three distinct shapes to their matching target zones by cycling through them one at a time. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the currently active shape; the spacebar switches focus to the next shape. RULE: The white dot always marks the center of the active shape, confirming which one you are controlling. TRAP: Assuming the white dot indicates your cursor or target location; it strictly identifies the active piece’s center.

GOAL: Turn every grid’s outer ring solid blue to unlock the framed panel. CONTROLS: Clicking any outer cell rotates that grid’s ring one step clockwise. RULE: Only the outer eight cells move; the center widget stays fixed as a reference. TRAP: I wasted time trying to flip colors directly, forgetting that rotation alone solves the pattern.

GOAL: Recreate the widget's pattern in the empty grid by toggling specific cells. CONTROLS: Clicking a grid cell toggles its color between blue and red. RULE: The central widget acts as a legend; white cells map to red, gray cells map to blue. TRAP: Assuming the widget changes when clicked; it is a static target, not an interactive control.

GOAL: Move two yellow tokens onto the two marked crosses. CONTROLS: Clicking a ring rotates it, shifting all tiles on that ring one step clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Tokens only move if they sit on the ring you rotate; otherwise, they stay put. TRAP: Thinking you must align rings perfectly first; instead, move one token to a shared junction to switch rings easily.

GOAL: Place the W-block and C-block into their matching dark outlines. CONTROLS: Click a block to select it; use arrow keys to move it one step. RULE: A block only fits an outline if its center letter matches the outline’s center. TRAP: Moving blindly without checking which block is selected wastes turns on the wrong piece.

GOAL: Guide the yellow dot along the left oval loop and the orange dot along the right loop to their finish lines. CONTROLS: Left click rotates the left loop clockwise; right click rotates the right loop counter-clockwise. RULE: Shared tiles at the top and bottom do not move, acting as fixed pivots for the rotation. TRAP: Assuming the diagonal tile is on the outer edge; it is actually part of the inner path, so do not expect it to shift when rotating the outer ring.

GOAL: Turn all grid cells orange. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color. RULE: White tiles match the widget center’s color; gray tiles are the opposite. TRAP: Assuming white always means orange, ignoring that it mirrors the changing center color.

ESTABLISHED: Both blocks reach the top corridor and merge uniquely at one position. The level does not clear upon merging there. FAILED: Moving both blocks to the top corridor and merging them did not trigger a win. GOAL IS NOT: Simply getting both blocks to the top corridor or merging them in the shared space. CONTROLS: RIGHT moves the left block right and the right block left simultaneously; LEFT reverses this motion.

ESTABLISHED: All four dial orientations on the plus tile fail. The block cannot currently reach the boxed area due to alignment or pathing errors in previous attempts. FAILED: Placing any dial combination on the plus tile. Moving the block to the corridor's end without entering the box. GOAL IS NOT: The plus tile itself. Simply standing at the corridor entrance. CONTROLS: Dials change block orientation. Movement shifts the block. The plus tile triggers checks but yields no victory.

GOAL: Turn all grid cells to the correct color by decoding the pattern overlays. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color through blue, red, and orange. RULE: White pattern cells take the center symbol’s color; gray cells become red. TRAP: Assuming gray meant "any non-center color" cost time; it strictly meant red.

GOAL: Learn the hidden movement cycles for yellow and orange tiles to reach their specific target cells. CONTROLS: Left-red rotates the horizontal loop; down-red rotates the vertical loop; clicks apply these rotations. RULE: Tiles on independent loops move separately; shared cells affect both, requiring careful sequencing to avoid undoing progress. TRAP: Assuming all tiles move together or that learning one loop resets the other wastes actions; track each cycle independently first.

GOAL: Slide the plug so its prongs align perfectly with the socket. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug; Space rotates it. RULE: Each arrow press moves the plug exactly three cells in that direction. TRAP: Assuming one press equals one cell causes constant overshooting and wasted turns.

ESTABLISHED: The black column is fixed; sliding stops exactly six steps. The red block cannot be pushed because the player never touches it. SPACE resets the player to the start and toggles the HUD indicator without altering walls. FAILED: Sliding further, pushing the red block, and pressing SPACE to change the maze layout. GOAL IS NOT: Moving the player to the target or physically pushing the red block. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player up to six steps. SPACE resets position and swaps the HUD icon.

GOAL: Match every cell’s color to the pattern dictated by nearby achromatic tiles. CONTROLS: Clicking a standard cell flips its color; clicking a magenta widget flips itself and its four orthogonal neighbors. RULE: Achromatic widgets define targets: 'c' means match center, 'g' means opposite, 'G' is ignored. TRAP: Assuming widget clicks affect all adjacent tiles; they skip non-cell widgets, limiting their range.

GOAL: Align the moving shape with the stationary yellow target outline. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the shape; the right panel mirrors the left panel’s movement across the central divider. RULE: Moving the left shape away from the divider moves the right shape away from it, maintaining symmetry. TRAP: Assuming the yellow shape moves with controls wastes actions; it is a fixed goal marker.

GOAL: Move the green token onto the yellow square to win. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicking buttons swaps colored blocks. RULE: Blue blocks become walkable floor, allowing you to cross gaps. TRAP: Do not assume yellow is a wall; it is the target, not an obstacle.

GOAL: Align the plug's yellow bar with the black bar's yellow slot. CONTROLS: Top blue button shifts walls and plug right; bottom blue button shifts them left. RULE: The plug only fits when its yellow section perfectly matches the gap's position. TRAP: Assuming the plug moves independently; it is locked to the bottom wall's movement.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to the exit using minimal steps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one cell at a time; pressing a key moves you exactly one square in that direction. RULE: Walls are solid barriers that stop movement; you cannot pass through or land on them. TRAP: Believing keys cause sliding until a wall. This false assumption caused wasted moves and confusion about grid connectivity.

GOAL: Slide the charcoal block directly onto the yellow square below. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; Space toggles the active axis. RULE: White dots on the block enable vertical movement; blue dots lock it to horizontal. TRAP: Assuming vertical movement is always available; you must toggle dots to white before pressing down.

GOAL: Slide the plug right to align with the distant slot. CONTROLS: Left button retreats the plug; right button advances it four spaces per press. RULE: The plug must align exactly with the slot's column in the upper bar. TRAP: The middle shelf moves opposite the plug, shrinking the space and risking a blockage before you reach the target.

GOAL: Trace the plug’s path to clear the level in exactly ten clicks. CONTROLS: Clicks toggle marks; the plug moves left or right based on active horizontal signals. RULE: A single active mark triggers one directional move, with the final jump back to start being a reset, not a game action. TRAP: Counting the return-to-start jump as a valid move inflates the action count and breaks the solution logic.

GOAL: Cross the deadly row to reach the exit on the right side. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one square in the chosen direction. RULE: The red enemy stayed asleep until you were within two steps, then lunged two spaces toward you. TRAP: Thinking the enemy was a static wall; it was a trap that killed you if you entered its wake range.

ESTABLISHED: The press tilts left, center, and right. Purple ink is selected. The canvas is currently all white. FAILED: Pressing without checking the specific tilt angle yields no useful shape data. Repeated presses on already-dyed areas provide no new information. GOAL IS NOT: Simply covering the canvas with any color. The specific shape of the ink deposit matters. CONTROLS: SPACE applies ink. RIGHT rotates the press. Clicking selects ink color.

GOAL: Guide the purple square to the blue circle by stepping through scattered dots. CONTROLS: Clicking any dot instantly teleports the square's center to that dot's location. RULE: The square ignores obstacles and walls, jumping directly to the clicked target. TRAP: Believing you must click dots in strict bottom-to-top order; clicking any visible dot works immediately.

GOAL: Move the plug to the pink target in the upper room. CONTROLS: Click green blocks to destroy them; use arrows to slide the plug. RULE: The plug can only climb through openings in the wall between rooms. TRAP: You cannot climb through solid walls; you must clear the green blocks first.

ESTABLISHED: Plug is at rows 28-31, facing left, prong at column 24. Socket S2 is at columns 20-23. S2 is highlighted, indicating readiness. FAILED: Capturing a single socket does not clear the level. Previous movement batches were inconsistent or rejected. GOAL IS NOT: Simply capturing one socket. CONTROLS: Left/Right/Up/Down moves the plug. Space captures the adjacent highlighted socket.

GOAL: Align mirror line and move pieces to cover four marked zones. CONTROLS: Arrows moved selected item; Space cycled selection between pieces and mirror. RULE: Pieces must land exactly on their targets so reflections hit remaining zones. TRAP: Moving mirror before positioning pieces caused misaligned reflections.

GOAL: Raise the plug to the lock by lowering the shafts just enough to fit. CONTROLS: Blue sinks the target shaft; Green sinks the plug shaft; Red raises the target shaft. RULE: You must alternate sinking and raising the target to keep it visible for the next sink. TRAP: Assuming you can sink the target twice in a row; the second click fails if the shaft is already too low.

GOAL: Place the divider on the target row to complete the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece. Space cycles selection between the divider and the two blocks. RULE: Only the selected piece responds to arrow keys; Space is required to switch focus. TRAP: Space often appears to do nothing because multiple pieces share the same target color, hiding the selection change.

GOAL: Guide a falling block into a specific cup. CONTROLS: Arrows shift a horizontal bar; Space triggers the block’s fall. RULE: The block lands on the bar if positioned correctly, allowing you to carry it horizontally before dropping it again. TRAP: Believing the block falls through the bar; it actually rests on top, requiring precise alignment to catch it.

ESTABLISHED: Each wheel has a unique seven-glyph cycle; Column 4’s cycle includes three top-row pink shapes. FAILED: Assuming all wheels share the same cyclic order or that the target is the untransformed partner shape. GOAL IS NOT: A simple horizontal mirror of the top row or a shared cycle phase across all wheels. CONTROLS: Rotating wheels cycles through glyphs; selecting a glyph checks it against the column’s specific transformation rule.

GOAL: Rotate five independent glyphs to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selection cursor; UP cycles the selected glyph forward. RULE: Each wheel operates independently; rotating one does not affect the others. TRAP: Assuming a global rotation affects all wheels simultaneously, causing wasted actions on incorrect adjustments.

GOAL: Arrange blocks to match the top outline's color sequence. CONTROLS: Click a bottom block to pick it up, then click a slot to drop it there. RULE: The top row defines the required left-to-right color order for the slots below. TRAP: Thinking you can drag blocks directly; you must click twice: once to select, once to place.

GOAL: Eliminate the vertical chasers to clear the path to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows move two spaces; landing on an enemy captures it. RULE: Vertical chasers ignore horizontal threats, making same-row approaches safe. TRAP: Assuming the lethal tile was a wall, not realizing it was just a danger zone you could pass through after clearing the threat.

GOAL: Align both the green and yellow dots exactly with their matching cross targets. CONTROLS: Click side arrows to move the green dot horizontally; click bottom arrows to move the yellow dot vertically. RULE: Dots must land precisely on the center of each cross; merely covering the area does not count. TRAP: Believing that overlapping the cross shape completes the level, rather than needing exact center alignment.

GOAL: Center each colored plus sign so its arms cover every matching dot on the board. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active plus by three spaces; the spacebar switches which plus is active. RULE: The active plus is split into four separate arms by a white center, while inactive pluses appear as solid shapes. TRAP: Believing the plus stops at the board's edge wasted time, as it can extend off-screen and be clipped.

GOAL: Place shapes into panels following a continuous path through the connector. CONTROLS: Click to move shapes, Space to check the solution, and Undo to revert mistakes. RULE: The connector defines a single snake-like route that dictates the strict order of slots. TRAP: Treating each panel as an independent puzzle ignores the connector’s role in linking the sequence.

GOAL: Align three colored shapes to cover matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Space switches focus. RULE: Shapes only reach grid spots where row and column numbers divide evenly by three. TRAP: Assuming any position works; checking divisibility by three prevents wasted moves.

GOAL: Place seven colored blocks into matching outlines across two panels linked by a central connector. CONTROLS: Click a slot to cycle through colors; press space to verify the current arrangement. RULE: The connector acts as a relay, routing the third color from the first panel directly into the second panel’s sequence. TRAP: Mistaking the connector’s endpoint for a fillable slot; it is a fixed node that cannot be clicked or colored.

GOAL: Place the purple blob’s red center inside the purple ring. CONTROLS: Click any two shapes to swap their positions instantly. RULE: Only the red center triggers the win; other centers do not count. TRAP: Thinking any object could fill the ring; only the specific red dot works.

GOAL: The level required pushing a large block into a designated black box to complete the puzzle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player character; walking into the block pushed it one tile in that direction. RULE: The block moves exactly one tile per push, allowing precise navigation around walls and into the target zone. TRAP: Assuming the block could slide continuously until hitting a wall cost time; it stops after a single step.

ESTABLISHED: Blocks attach to the trail at their column positions. The trail is horizontal, so it can only collect blocks sharing the same row unless moved. FAILED: Moving the trail vertically while blocks remain stacked in one column causes the attached block to push the next, blocking collection. GOAL IS NOT: Simply dragging the trail through a vertical stack to collect all blocks simultaneously. CONTROLS: LEFT shrinks the trail, pulling attached blocks left. RIGHT extends the trail to capture new blocks. UP and DOWN move the entire trail vertically.

GOAL: Fill all seven panel slots with blocks matching their hidden colors. CONTROLS: Click a tray block to select it, then click a slot to place it; press space to check the solution. RULE: The green panel’s pre-placed block hints that the green tray item is a valid, placeable piece. TRAP: Assuming the green hollow block is a decorative key rather than a standard placeable block.

GOAL: Guide two separate blocks to merge into one single shape. CONTROLS: Use arrow keys to move both blocks simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Blocks slide until hitting walls or each other, causing them to stick together upon contact. TRAP: Assuming merging ends the level; the combined shape often requires further movement to reach the true target.

GOAL: Place three shapes to cover scattered dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches to the next shape. RULE: Shapes are rigid, so their fixed geometry must align perfectly with the dot patterns. TRAP: Assuming shapes resize; they do not, requiring exact center placement to match fixed spans and arms.

GOAL: Guide the yellow marker to the starting index by rotating the ring. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the ring in one direction. RULE: Each click rotates the ring by one position toward the target. TRAP: Assuming the green arrow was necessary; the red arrow alone solved the puzzle.

ESTABLISHED: Matching shrinks the tip to 2x2; a second match expands it back. The panel resets to empty after matching. FAILED: Moving the large tip left through the notch fails because it is too wide to fit. GOAL IS NOT: Simply rotating the tip or filling the panel with colors. CONTROLS: Click cells to place colors. Match to resize the tip. Left/Right move the tip horizontally.

GOAL: Shrink colored bars to minimum length to reset the puzzle state. CONTROLS: Clicking left shrinks bars; clicking right extends them. RULE: The harness halts all subsequent actions immediately after any no-op click. TRAP: Assuming batched clicks continue; a single wasted click stops the entire sequence.

GOAL: Recover scattered dots by matching each emitter’s color to its target dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected emitter; Space toggles between the X and plus shapes. RULE: An emitter only recovers a dot if its current color matches the dot’s original hue. TRAP: Moving an already-colored emitter over a palette changes its color; don’t assume it stays fixed while passing through.

GOAL: Align the moving tip with the fixed handle. CONTROLS: Arrows shift the tip; clicks deal cards to trigger matches. RULE: Matches only succeed when the tip is perfectly docked against the handle. TRAP: Assuming the first click after a reset registers; it often fails, requiring a retry.

GOAL: Compress the wide plug tip so it fits through the narrow neck and reaches the handle. CONTROLS: Click keypad cells to match the dot pattern; use arrow keys to move the plug vertically along the track. RULE: Matching the pattern shrinks the plug’s width, allowing it to pass through the charcoal-marked neck. TRAP: Trying to push the wide tip through the neck without first shrinking it via the keypad.

GOAL: Align specific symbols in the vertical column and two horizontal rows to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Red and green arrows shift the vertical column up or down; side arrows shift the top and bottom rows left or right. RULE: Each arrow rotates its line’s contents by one position, wrapping around the ends like a conveyor belt. TRAP: Assuming arrow colors dictate direction universally; here, red shifts the column differently than row arrows, requiring careful tracking of each line’s orientation.

GOAL: Guide two squares to their goals without hitting red hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows move both squares simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: If either square touches a red cell, both instantly reset to the start. TRAP: Assuming blocks stop movement; they actually trigger a full reset for both pieces.

GOAL: Map hidden slot colors to their correct outlines to clear the level. CONTROLS: Click to place blocks in slots; press Space to validate the current arrangement. RULE: Validation checks slots sequentially; the first mismatch reveals the expected color at that position. TRAP: Assuming connectors override color requirements; they do not, so empty or mismatched slots still fail validation.

GOAL: Clear the board by reducing all pieces to a single survivor. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, then click a destination to jump over an adjacent piece. RULE: A valid move requires jumping over a neighboring piece into an empty spot, removing the jumped piece. TRAP: Assuming you can jump to any empty space; you must strictly land exactly two steps away over a neighbor.

GOAL: Make the bottom-right panel match the target pattern shown by the arrow. CONTROLS: Click a cell to toggle its color between blue and red. RULE: The arrow points to the specific quadrant whose pattern is the correct solution. TRAP: Assuming the goal was to make all quadrants identical or turn everything blue.

GOAL: Slide the plug so its prongs fit into the socket beside the green wall. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug one step; rotation keys turn it to match the socket. RULE: The plug must sit flush against the green surface with tips covering the red contacts. TRAP: Assuming the plug inserts inside the green; it only fits in the empty space to the left.

GOAL: Move Yellow and Orange to their target slots without colliding at the shared center. CONTROLS: Left and Right buttons rotate their respective sides clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: Yellow is blocked if it lands on the shared indices (3 or 7) while Orange is active. TRAP: Ignoring the shared-cell conflict causes rotations to pull Yellow out of position, wasting moves.

GOAL: Place the green block so its white dot aligns with the center of the charcoal ring. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active block; clicks switch between blocks. RULE: Blocks slide until hitting an obstacle, then stop adjacent to it. TRAP: Assuming you could step into the ring’s center; you cannot overlap the charcoal frame.

GOAL: Cover both target rings by repositioning the moving head to the correct spots. CONTROLS: Clicking a ring moves the head to it; clicking the head moves it to a new position. RULE: The blob’s size stays fixed, so you must plan a two-step path to dodge obstacles. TRAP: Believing the head must stay in one color chain; switching chains early is required to reach both targets.

GOAL: Match the grid to the hidden spinner patterns by toggling cells between orange and blue. CONTROLS: Click a cell to switch its color, aiming to align rows with the spinner’s top, middle, and bottom lines. RULE: Each spinner dictates a specific color pattern for its corresponding panel; all cells must match simultaneously. TRAP: Assuming every visible dot is a target; some cells are wildcards or require inverse logic, causing wasted clicks on wrong colors.

GOAL: Fit blocks into ring-shaped holes. CONTROLS: Arrows slide blocks; clicks select targets. RULE: Blocks stop at holes or walls, ignoring inner gaps. TRAP: Assuming holes are solid; they have centers that do not block sliding.

GOAL: Rotate yellow and orange tokens to their target slots in the center. CONTROLS: Click top or bottom arrows to spin the vertical ring. Click left or right arrows to spin the horizontal ring. RULE: Each click shifts all tokens on that ring by one position in the arrow’s direction. TRAP: Assuming horizontal moves affect vertical-only tokens, or vice versa, wastes moves. Tokens only shift when on the clicked ring.

GOAL: Recolor specific grid cells to match the hub colors projected by four edge spinners. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color between red and orange.
